figureObjective: Show heat flow from a hot reservoir through a cyclic heat engine to work output and rejected heat at a cold reservoir.

claims.text: A heat engine uses part of the energy transferred from a hot source to do work.
Qh flows from the hot reservoir into the engine, W leaves as work output, and Qc leaves the engine for the cold reservoir.
For a complete cycle, internal energy returns to its original value and the work output is W = Qh - Qc.
Thermal efficiency is Eff = W / Qh and cannot be represented as perfect heat-to-work conversion for this heat-engine mechanism.
No numeric energy is required; if values are later shown, Qh, Qc, and W must use one consistent energy unit.

elements.meaning: High-temperature reservoir Th supplying heat Qh.
Cyclic working system that converts part of Qh into work.
Low-temperature reservoir Tc receiving rejected heat Qc.
Heat transfer Qh from the hot reservoir to the engine.
Useful work W leaving the engine.
Unused heat Qc leaving the engine for the cold reservoir.

allowedVariation.rule: Reservoirs may be stacked or arranged left-to-right if Qh, W, and Qc directions remain explicit.
Hot and cold colors may vary if labels Th and Tc and all energy-flow labels remain readable.

mutations.description: Delete Qc and show Qh = W, implying perfect conversion of heat to work.
Reverse Qh or Qc while continuing to label the device as a heat engine.
Point W into the engine or attach Qh and Qc to the wrong reservoirs.
